*Settling in to think it through, as the farmer*

Let me think about this year. These 3 mu are everything we have — me and my husband, that's all our household now. Our boy is in the city; he sends a little money sometimes but the land is my job. I've been doing this since I was a girl, and for maybe thirty years it's been the same pattern: wheat in autumn, maize in summer. That's what works here, that's what everyone does. I don't want to try anything clever at my age.

Last year the wheat was okay — maybe 800 jin per mu, nothing special but nothing bad either. The maize was good, around 900 jin. Prices weren't great but they weren't terrible. I used the same fertilizer I always use — one bag of the green-bag compound (the 15-15-15 one) per mu before sowing, then some urea in spring when the wheat starts to stand up. Same for the maize. My neighbor Old Wang tried putting on less urea two years ago and his wheat went yellow, so I stick with what I know.

Money is tight. The compound fertilizer went up again this year, my daughter-in-law told me on the phone. I'll still buy what I need but I'm not going to add extra. A bag per mu is enough. If the wheat looks weak in spring I'll put on a bit more urea, maybe ten kilos per mu — that's about how much everyone does.

For work, I can't do what I used to. I can sow and weed and watch the fields, but the tilling and the harvest — my husband and I pay the neighbor with the tractor. He charges us a fair price because we're old. For the maize, we don't till at all anymore — you just plant right into the wheat stubble after harvest, everyone does it this way now, it saves time. That wheat-to-maize turnaround is only a few days.

Irrigation — I pay for the well water, it's not free. For wheat I need to give it water before winter sets in, and again in spring when it's jointing. If it's a dry year I'll do one more before the grain fills out. For maize, usually the summer rain is enough, but if July is dry I'll irrigate once. I don't want to pay for water I don't need, but I also don't want to lose the crop — we can't afford a bad year.

Pests — I spray herbicide for the weeds, that's a must. Insects I don't bother with unless I see something. The maize sometimes gets borers but one spray is enough if it's bad.

That's my plan. Same as last year, same as the year before. At my age I'm not going to change things.
